newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail awaits Clifford Bay appeals.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail awaits Clifford Bay appeals.

text.p: Tranz Rail directors will wait for any appeals before deciding whether to go ahead with a ferry terminal at Clifford Bay, south of Blenheim, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.
Tranz Rail was given planning permission for the terminal on Wednesday by Marlborough District Council.
A NZ$500 million plan involves new terminals in Wellington and Clifford Bay, with three new ferries.
If the Tranz Rail board of directors decides to proceed with the terminal, and no appeals are made against the decision, the terminal could be open for business within three years.
Tranz Rail spokesman Fred Cockram said that though Tranz Rail had shown it was interested in the Clifford Bay site, it could decide to delay the move from Picton.
Cockram has said the new ferries Tranz Rail wanted to buy were too big for the Picton terminal. New berthing facilities would also have to be built in Wellington.
Tranz Rail is negotiating with Ports of Wellington and Wellington City Council over a move from Kaiwharawhara to Glasgow Wharf.
Marlborough Mayor Liz Davidson said today's decision had about 200 pages of conditions Tranz Rail must fulfil.
"It may not yet go ahead," she said. "Tranz Rail haven't seen the conditions; they may have to do their sums again and think about it."
The conditions are expected to relate to public access to the coast near the terminal, sediment management and water circulation in nearby Lake Grassmere.
Davidson said reaction to the decision varied around the Marlborough district.

Tranz Rail has said a new port at Clifford Bay would shorten the sea voyage from Wellington to the South Island by 30 minutes. Because Clifford Bay is farther south than Picton, road freight and trains could get to Christchurch quicker.
